title: The Well
logline: A well-digger spends weeks making something that is only empty space, and a village names the hole, and depends on it.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From the salt water the boat works on to the fresh water a village waits for: after a thing that stays 'the same' while every part changes, a thing that is named though it is only empty space.

thread_out.thread: Water carries across: from a well's first water to a tasting room where cups of tea are smelled, tasted and graded, a name built only from the senses.

requirements: A well dug during the filming window
Safe camera access around and possibly into the shaft
A family for whom the well matters

lesson.in_simple_terms: A well is named for what is not there: it is an empty space left where earth was dug out. A village gives that emptiness a name, relies on it and draws water from it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ළිඳක් යනු පස් හාරා ඉවත් කළ තැන ඉතිරි වූ හිස් අවකාශයකට අප දෙන නමක් වන අතර, ඒ හිස්කමට නමක් දී ගම්මානය එය මත යැපේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the concepts (paññatti) the texts list is the concept of space (ākāsa-paññatti): wells and caves, named by an emptiness rather than by anything present. The texts contrast concepts with the ultimate realities, which they describe not as lumps of stuff but as momentary forces or activities. Matter (rūpa) is described as what is struck and altered by opposing conditions such as cold and heat; the name 'well' is given to a gap among these changing material processes.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows the digger down into the earth: buckets of soil rising, heat and echo, the circle of light above shrinking as the space below grows. When the first water seeps in and the family draws from it, the viewer sees a whole household depending on something made by taking away, and a name given to the emptiness itself.

key_terms.en: concept of space: a well, a cave, named by emptiness
materiality; that which is altered by opposing conditions such as cold and heat

lesson.caution: This does not mean the well or its water is unreal, and the earth and water in the film are not being presented as the texts' technical 'great elements'; the film only notices that the name points to a space, not a substance.
lesson.builds_on: The boat kept its name while its parts changed; the well goes further, because it is named for a space where there are no parts at all.
